title: Powered by God's Love Gift (Ps Mark Ng)

messages.text: Through Christ's death, God presents you "holy, and blameless, and above reproach in His sight."
messages.explanation:
You were once far from God, an enemy in your mind through wicked works. "Yet now He has reconciled you in the body of His flesh through death, to present you holy, and blameless, and above reproach in His sight." Not someday: now. God made the peace and finished it, through the blood of the cross.

Yesterday's quarrel with your spouse isn't on God's record. "Their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more," and in Greek that's a double negative: never, ever. Paul says to "continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast." Wake up each day believing you're holy in Christ, because that's how He sees you.

messages.text: God set up the network from heaven at Pentecost, and it can never be disconnected.
messages.explanation:
A father buys his daughter a phone so she can reach him whenever she needs help, and because he loves hearing her voice. "If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!"

Fifty days after the resurrection, "there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting." Sitting, at rest. Every one of them received. The connection between you and your Father was established by the blood of Jesus, and nothing can cut it.

messages.text: "Bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things." And Paul defines godliness as the gospel.
messages.explanation:
Paul uses the word "exercise": training, like lifting weights. On the first day you don't see muscles, but you keep going because you expect results. Then he says exercise yourself toward godliness, and he tells us what godliness is: "Great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit… received up in glory." It's Jesus and His finished work.

So exercise in the gospel: hear it, take Communion, declare "I am the righteousness of God in Christ," pray in the Spirit. If you're out for a morning walk anyway, pray as you go. Charging your phone profits a little; charging your inner man profits much.

messages.text: "No one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit." If you can confess it, you're not receiving an evil spirit.
messages.explanation:
Some people hesitate to pray in tongues because they're afraid: "What if it's not the Holy Spirit?" Paul settles it: "No one speaking by the Spirit of God calls Jesus accursed, and no one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit." If Jesus is your Lord, the Spirit in you is His.

And when it sounds like baby talk, remember a father's joy when his infant first manages "Pa-pa." He doesn't critique the pronunciation; he delights in the voice. "If I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays." Open your mouth by faith. Your Father loves to hear you.

messages.text: A saint is someone the Son shines through.
messages.explanation:
A teacher took her class into a cathedral and asked what a saint was. One little girl looked up at the stained-glass windows, lit up by the sun streaming through them, and said, "A saint is someone who lets the light shine through."

In Christ, every believer is a saint. "You are complete in Him, who is the head of all principality and power." When people ask why your family is blessed or how you stay calm, the answer is Him, shining through you, often without you even trying. Don't climb the corporate ladder at the cost of your health and family. Rest in His love; He'll lift you where you need to be.
